subject: Science
title: Me and my body
objectives: Children will point to and name main parts of the body.
Children will show what different body parts can do.
content: Naming main body parts, finding out what the body can do, and singing body songs.
teachingActivities: Touch each body part as you name it; use a mirror so children see their own body; sing and move together; use the same words every day.
learnerActivities: Point to and name body parts and show what each part can do.
assessment: Observe whether each child points to at least six body parts when named.
expectedOutcomes: Points to at least six body parts when named.
Says what a body part can do with support.

lessons.title: Head, hands and feet
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will point to and name the head, hands and feet.
successCriteria: Points to the head, hands and feet when named
Says a body part name with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children are new to the class; they know some body parts from home and enjoy songs and movement.
lessons.starter: Sit in front of the mirror, touch your head and say "This is my head." Ask each child to touch their own head.
teacherActivities: Touch your head, hands and feet in turn and say each name clearly.
Say a body part and wait for children to find it on themselves.
Show the parts on the doll and ask "Where are the doll’s feet?"
Let each child look in the mirror and name one part.
learnerActivities: Children touch the same part on their own body.
Children touch the part named.
Child points to the doll’s feet.
Child touches a part and says its name.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Touch your head, hands and feet in turn and say each name clearly. Children: Children touch the same part on their own body.
Step 2. Teacher: Say a body part and wait for children to find it on themselves. Children: Children touch the part named.
Step 3. Teacher: Show the parts on the doll and ask "Where are the doll’s feet?" Children: Child points to the doll’s feet.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child look in the mirror and name one part. Children: Child touches a part and says its name.

practical.title: Mirror body parts
steps: Sit children in front of the mirror in small groups.
Name a body part and let them touch it.
practical.safety: Fix the mirror firmly to the wall or hold it steady so it cannot fall. Use an unbreakable mirror and keep children seated.

differentiation.support: Touch the part together on the child’s body and say the word.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to name a part and touch it on a friend’s doll.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Points to head, hands and feet
Names a body part with support
lessons.conclusion: Wave your hands, wiggle your feet and say "Thank you, body."
lessons.homeConnection: At bath time, touch each body part with your child and name it.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "point to and name the head, hands and feet" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Head, hands, feet, head, hands, feet. This is me.

lessons.title: Eyes, ears and mouth
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will point to and name the eyes, ears, nose and mouth.
successCriteria: Points to the eyes, ears, nose and mouth
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children are new to the class; they know some body parts from home and enjoy songs and movement.
lessons.starter: Point to your eyes and say "These are my eyes." Wink and ask "Where are your eyes?"
teacherActivities: Touch each part of your face and say its name: eyes, ears, nose, mouth.
Say a part of the face and wait.
Sing "Eyes, ears, nose and mouth" while touching each part.
Ask each child to point to a part on the doll’s face.
learnerActivities: Children touch the same part on their own face.
Children touch the part named.
Children touch and sing along.
Child points and says the name.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Touch each part of your face and say its name: eyes, ears, nose, mouth. Children: Children touch the same part on their own face.
Step 2. Teacher: Say a part of the face and wait. Children: Children touch the part named.
Step 3. Teacher: Sing "Eyes, ears, nose and mouth" while touching each part. Children: Children touch and sing along.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask each child to point to a part on the doll’s face. Children: Child points and says the name.

practical.title: Face parts
steps: Sit in front of the mirror.
Touch each face part as it is named.
Make a funny face and name the parts.
practical.safety: Remind children to touch their faces gently and keep fingers away from eyes. Use a steady, unbreakable mirror.

differentiation.support: Touch the part on your own face first and let the child copy.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to name a part and say what it does.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Names a face part with support
lessons.conclusion: Blow a kiss and say "Thank you, face."
lessons.homeConnection: Play touch your nose, ears and mouth at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "point to and name the eyes, ears, nose and mouth" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Eyes, ears, nose and mouth. This is my face.

lessons.title: What can my hands do?
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will show things that hands, feet and mouths can do.
successCriteria: Does an action with their hands
Says what a body part does with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children are new to the class; they know some body parts from home and enjoy songs and movement.
lessons.starter: Wave your hands and say "My hands can wave." Ask "What can your hands do?"
teacherActivities: Show an action for each body part: clap hands, stamp feet, blink eyes, sing with the mouth.
Say "What can hands do?" and show a ball, scarf and cup.
Say "What can feet do?" and let children stamp, walk and tiptoe.
Ask each child to show you something their body can do.
learnerActivities: Children copy each action.
Child picks up an object and uses their hands.
Children do the actions.
Child shows an action.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show an action for each body part: clap hands, stamp feet, blink eyes, sing with the mouth. Children: Children copy each action.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "What can hands do?" and show a ball, scarf and cup. Children: Child picks up an object and uses their hands.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "What can feet do?" and let children stamp, walk and tiptoe. Children: Children do the actions.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask each child to show you something their body can do. Children: Child shows an action.

practical.title: Body can do
steps: Clear a space on the mat.
Call a body part and let children show an action.
practical.safety: Clear the floor so children do not trip. Keep actions gentle and stop if anyone is tired.

differentiation.support: Do the action together and say the word.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to invent a new thing a body part can do.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Shows what body parts can do
Says what a part does with support
lessons.conclusion: Wave, clap and stamp together and then sit still.
lessons.homeConnection: Ask your child what their hands and feet can do while you do daily tasks.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show things that hands, feet and mouths can do" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: The body song
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will sing a body song and touch each part.
successCriteria: Touches the right body part in the song
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children are new to the class; they know some body parts from home and enjoy songs and movement.
lessons.starter: Say "Let us sing about our body." Touch your head and tap the drum once.
teacherActivities: Sing "Head, shoulders, knees and toes" slowly with actions.
Sing again and speed up a little.
Sing again and leave out a word.
Let a child lead the song with the doll.
learnerActivities: Children touch each part.
Children keep up with the actions.
Children touch the part and say the word.
Child touches the doll and the group copies.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing "Head, shoulders, knees and toes" slowly with actions. Children: Children touch each part.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing again and speed up a little. Children: Children keep up with the actions.
Step 3. Teacher: Sing again and leave out a word. Children: Children touch the part and say the word.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child lead the song with the doll. Children: Child touches the doll and the group copies.

practical.title: Sing and touch
steps: Sing the song and touch each part.
Sing it quickly and then slowly.
practical.safety: Leave space around each child. Stop and sit down when children are tired.

differentiation.support: Sing softly and touch the part together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead the song and choose the part.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Sing the song quietly and sit down.
lessons.homeConnection: Sing the body song at home and touch each part.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sing a body song and touch each part" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Head, shoulders, knees and toes, knees and toes.

lessons.title: Week 1 body check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child names body parts and shows what they can do.
successCriteria: Points to at least six body parts
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children are new to the class; they know some body parts from home and enjoy songs and movement.
lessons.starter: Sing the body song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: mirror, doll and song.
At each station name a body part and ask the child to point to it.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child points to the part.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: mirror, doll and song. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station name a body part and ask the child to point to it. Children: Child points to the part.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Body stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use an unbreakable mirror held steady.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use three body parts.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to name parts for a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: points to body parts when named; names a part; shows what a part can do.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 1
Points to at least six body parts
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye with hands and feet.
lessons.homeConnection: Name body parts at home during dressing and bathing.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child names body parts and shows what they can do" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
